source.publication: Rhode Island Retirement Income Tax Guide, Publication 2026-01 (tax year 2025)
source.section: Instructions PDF pp.9-10, Schedule M line 1t, questions 1 and 2 and table lines 1-4; Worksheet Step 1 lines 1-7, Step 2 lines 8-13 and instructions PDF p.9, Schedule M line 1s; Instructions PDF p.10, Schedule M line 1v; Guide PDF p.15; Guide PDF pp.24-26, Section 5 Example #10; Instructions PDF p.4, RI-1040 lines 1-5; PDF p.5, lines 6-8; PDF p.13, Tax Computation Worksheet ('Use for all filing status types')

worked: Federal AGI = wages 50,000.00 + military pension (person 1) 4,500.00 + annuity (person 0) 5,500.00 + IRA distributions 10,000.00 + employer plan distributions 10,000.00 + taxable Social Security 10,000.00 = 90,000.00. Federal taxable income = 90,000.00 - 31,500.00 standard deduction - 1 x 1,600.00 age 65+ = 56,900.00 (given, not tested; federal senior deduction ignored). RI-1040 line 1 federal AGI 90,000.00. Line 1s, Social Security worksheet: person 0 born 1957-06-15 (age 68), person 1 born 1961-06-15 (age 64). Line 3 federal AGI 90,000.00; line 4 Married filing jointly; line 5 born on or before 03/01/1959: yes; line 6 133,750.00; line 7 90,000.00 less than 133,750.00: yes. Line 8 benefits 11,764.70; line 9 attributed to the person born on or before 03/01/1959 7,058.82; line 10 = 0.6000; line 12 = 0.6000. Line 11 taxable benefits 10,000.00; line 13 = 10,000.00 x 0.6000 = 6,000.00. Line 1t: question 1 born on or before March 1, 1959: person 0 born 1957-06-15 (age 68), person 1 born 1961-06-15 (age 64): yes; question 2 federal AGI 90,000.00 less than or equal to 133,750.00: yes. Table: person 0 line 2 13,500.00, line 3 lesser of that and 50,000.00 = 13,500.00; person 1 line 2 0.00, line 3 lesser of that and 50,000.00 = 0.00; line 4 = 13,500.00. Line 1v military service pension 4,500.00 (in full, no age or income test). Line 1y total decreasing modifications = 24,000.00. Line 2a other-state obligations 0.00; line 2m total increasing modifications = 0.00. Schedule M page 2 line 3 net = 0.00 - 24,000.00 = -24,000.00; RI-1040 line 2 = -24,000.00. Line 3 modified federal AGI = 90,000.00 + (-24,000.00) = 66,000.00. Standard Deduction and Exemption Worksheets: line 3 66,000.00 is not more than 254,250.00: the worksheets stop at line 3, full amounts. Line 4 standard deduction: 21,800.00 (Married filing jointly). Line 5 = 66,000.00 - 21,800.00 = 44,200.00. Line 6 exemptions: 2 x 5,100.00 = 10,200.00. Line 7 taxable income = 44,200.00 - 10,200.00 = 34,000.00. Line 8 tax on 34,000.00 by the schedule as numbers: 34,000.00 x 0.0375 = 1275.0000000 = 1,275.00. Credits 0.00 (Schedule I, Schedule II, RI earned income credit and RI-1040H are not modelled and not claimed here). Rhode Island income tax = 1,275.00. Note: Guide Example #10 (Frank 68, Judy 64; federal AGI 90,000): the Guide's total is 24,000 (13,500 + 6,000 + 4,500). Her 401(k) fails on age, her military pay needs no age. The wages and IRA are given to Frank; the Guide does not split them and they don't matter. Gross benefits are set to give the Guide's 6,000 of 10,000 (share 0.6000, total at 85% = 10,000.00).
accepted_approximations: On a joint return with one qualifying person, the Social Security subtraction is the taxable benefits times that person's share of total benefits (worksheet lines 8-12). Consumers must divide taxable Social Security between the spouses by their gross benefits to get this result.
